data.narrative:
StoreDot is a Series E climate and energy company that has raised $206.5M to date. The valuation landscape in Climate & Energy includes 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lilium, LNZA), though narrow peer cohorts at identical stage and valuation tier proved too sparse to support a robust median-multiple approach.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.4x multiplier to the $206M total-raised proxy, implying a $289M valuation. This method reflects typical step-up dynamics for Series E financings in the sector. Peer-median methodology was not applicable given only two adjacent-stage comparables and zero same-stage peers within sufficiently tight filters; a broader sector median would lack specificity to StoreDot's position. The existing public comp (Lilium) and private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBolt Metals, and Electric Hydrogen represent the broader Climate & Energy universe but do not provide statistically reliable controls for direct multiple imputation.

The triangulation supports a range of $246M (low) to $332M (high), with a median of $289M. This represents a 15–61% premium to total capital deployed, consistent with Series E stage dynamics. Key uncertainties include StoreDot's technology-readiness level and path to commercialization relative to peers, battery-chemistry differentiation, and near-term customer validation—factors not captured in raised-capital proxies alone.
